evidence.craft: Read src/selfrep_terminal/model.py (46 lines), tests/test_terminal.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. Small and clear; the closed form handles the three regimes. Defects: the sibling model is reached by sys.path.insert at import time (model.py:16-17), and the test imports selfrep_reinvest only through that side effect (tests/test_terminal.py:7); pyproject.toml declares no dependencies though the package cannot import without three sibling trees (the README states this). best_switch ignores the n0 that value() accepts. figure.py parses results.txt rather than retyping numbers, which is good practice.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'within 1 h of T - 1/k + s/a' (results.txt, all rows, max gap 0.5 h) backed; ts = 550..600 backed; threshold 50/62.5/83.3 and 29/37/49% backed and recomputed; 97.4/91.1/73.8% backed by results.txt (Euler model; analytic 97.35/90.98/73.58); Euler 97.1-97.3% and 98.1-99.1% backed; '6 tests' and '~20 s' backed; 'not a new result' and 'every input is assumed' are honest limits; AI-assistance note present. The homepage summary (research/_homepage/projects.json) repeats the same numbers ('costs 3-26%'). The live page returned a proxy 403 (`curl ... CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`); served-copy.mjs says it is not a product page, so the served page was not loaded. One limitation is stale or understated: 'there is no dynamic-programming certificate for this objective' (README:30), while the problem's value function is linear in N, so a three-line costate/DP argument (reproduced by this audit's DP) certifies global optimality, and the sibling selfrep-terminalmarket and selfrep-exactdp later did the DP.
evidence.fitness: Could a researcher build on it? Yes, and two siblings (selfrep-terminalmarket, selfrep-exactdp) did. Nearest prior work: the linear bang-bang allocation problem with a salvage value is textbook optimal control (Sethi and Thompson, Optimal Control Theory, linear investment/consumption models with salvage value; Kamien and Schwartz, Dynamic Optimization) and the same 'switch one e-folding time before the end' result is classic in life-history theory (Macevicz and Oster 1976 on worker-to-reproductive switching in annual colonies; Cohen 1971). The README honestly says the result is elementary and not new, but cites none of this literature, so a reader cannot see the result is a known one. Sound but not new and not publishable alone; as a step it is below the research/CLAUDE.md programme bar (a separate slug rather than a step inside a programme).
evidence.domain: Against Pontryagin's principle: H = a(1-u)N + lam k u N, lam(T) = s, switching function k lam - a; integrating backward gives the switch at T - 1/k + s/a and never switching when s >= a/k, exactly the README's formula, and the DP over all policies agrees. The method would be signed off; the practitioner would note (a) global optimality is provable here, so the 'only the copy-then-switch family is checked' caveat is weaker than necessary, and (b) the percentages quoted are of the Euler discretisation (step 0.25 h, ~2.7% value bias) rather than of the stated continuous model.

verdict: A small, correct and honest step in the self-replicating-shop track. Its closed form (goods phase 1/k - s/a, never switch once s >= a/k) matches a hand Pontryagin derivation, and an independent backward DP over every policy of the discrete model reproduces the grid optimum (e.g. 2,912,767.8 at fail 0, s 0) with copy-then-switch structure in all 18 cases; the experiment and figure reproduce byte-identically. It misses the bar on verification: two of four seeded mutants in closed_form's goods-only branch survive the six tests. As research it is sound but not new: the salvage-value bang-bang switch is textbook optimal control and classic life-history theory, which the README admits is elementary but does not cite, and its 'no DP certificate' limitation understates what a three-line argument proves.
